name: Tampere University
summary: Multidisciplinary university in Tampere; 11 English bachelor's in engineering, science and urban and social studies, each a 3+2 path to a master's.

ib.text: IB holders apply in admission group II, ranked on certificate scores, and may also enter group I with an SAT/ACT. An IB Diploma completed in English, English A, or English B at 5 proves your English.

programmes.name: Automation and Robotics, Science and Engineering
programmes.about: Automation and robotics for many industries, from intelligent systems to machines, combining theory with hands-on learning; admits you to a 3+2 bachelor's and master's.
programmes.overview: You study mathematics, natural sciences and engineering foundations, then focus on designing and developing automation and robotic systems, programming intelligent machines and applying data, sensing and digital technologies to real problems; a minor subject complements your specialisation in the second year. Learning combines theory with projects, laboratory exercises and real engineering problems, with company collaboration and practical assignments, and second-year students can join research groups through research training placements. Graduates find work in manufacturing, energy, transport, healthcare and logistics, and the bachelor's degree leads straight into master's programmes at the same university without a new application.

programmes.name: Biomedical Engineering, Science and Engineering
programmes.about: Engineering and life sciences combined to develop new medical technologies, with lab work and research-based teaching; admits you to a 3+2 bachelor's and master's.
programmes.overview: The programme combines engineering, biology and health sciences, with a focus on biomedical instrumentation, biomaterials, tissue engineering and molecular biology. The first year covers mathematics and natural sciences, and the second introduces the biomedical engineering specialisation plus a minor of your choice. You learn through projects, laboratory exercises and real engineering problems, build teamwork skills, and can join research groups through research training placements. Graduates go into healthcare technology, medical device development, and research and innovation, and the bachelor's degree continues to several master's programmes at the same university without reapplication.

programmes.name: Chemistry, Science and Engineering
programmes.about: Analytical and experimental chemistry for sustainable energy, climate and advanced materials, with hands-on lab research and room to tailor your degree.
programmes.overview: You study organic, inorganic, physical, analytical and materials chemistry together with physics, mathematics and computational methods, taking an interdisciplinary approach to scientific problems. Teaching combines theory with hands-on experimentation, collaborative projects, laboratory exercises and research-oriented coursework, and in the second year you can join active research groups through research training placements. The programme draws on the university's Chemistry and Advanced Materials research centre. Graduates work in research institutions, high-technology industries, pharmaceuticals and environmental consulting, and the degree continues into master's programmes in chemistry and materials science without reapplication.

programmes.name: Computing Sciences and Electrical Engineering
programmes.about: Information technology, electrical engineering and computational data analysis in three study tracks, continuing straight to a Tampere master's without reapplying.
programmes.overview: You study programming, data analysis, mathematical modelling and intelligent systems on a base of mathematics and physics, and choose a major in Information Technology, Electrical Engineering or Computational Data Analysis, with specialisations such as signal processing and machine learning, software development, power engineering, communications or embedded systems. Teaching mixes theory with projects, laboratory exercises and real engineering problems, and second-year students can join research groups through research training placements. The bachelor's continues directly into master's programmes at the same university, towards fields such as machine learning, telecommunications and renewable energy.

programmes.name: Engineering Physics, Science and Engineering
programmes.about: Fundamental physics applied to engineering through modelling, computation and experiments, building analytical skills that transfer to many fields.
programmes.overview: You study the principles behind physical phenomena together with mathematics, modelling and computation, building foundations in mathematics, natural sciences and engineering in the first year before specialising in engineering physics with electives. Three focus areas are available: aerosol physics, computational physics and photonics. Teaching combines theory with projects, laboratory exercises and real engineering problems, and second-year students can join research groups for hands-on research experience. Graduates work in research, technology development, engineering design and data analysis, and the degree continues into master's programmes at the same university without reapplication.

programmes.name: Environmental Engineering, Science and Engineering
programmes.about: Environmental engineering on a solid theoretical base with lab work and projects, towards careers in sustainability, water management and industry.
programmes.overview: The first year covers mathematics, natural sciences and engineering, after which you specialise in environmental engineering: water treatment, wastewater management, resource efficiency, circular economy solutions, environmental monitoring, life cycle assessment and environmental modelling. You choose a minor that matches your interests, and learn through projects, laboratory exercises and real engineering problems, with research training placements available in the second year. Graduates work in environmental consulting, water and wastewater management, sustainable industry, environmental technology development and research, and the degree continues into master's programmes at the same university without reapplication.

programmes.name: Materials Science, Science and Engineering
programmes.about: Natural sciences and materials expertise for developing more durable, sustainable and recyclable materials across industries.
programmes.overview: You study how the structure of materials shapes their properties and performance, and how to design materials for specific uses, drawing on chemistry, physics and engineering for applications in renewable energy, medical devices, electronics and sustainable manufacturing. Teaching combines theory with projects, laboratory exercises and real engineering problems, in small multicultural groups using modern laboratory equipment and digital tools, and second-year students can join research groups through research training placements. Graduates work in high-tech manufacturing, energy solutions, research, product development and sustainability innovation, or continue directly to master's programmes at the same university.

programmes.name: Administrative Sciences, Sustainable Urban Development
programmes.about: Administrative sciences for urban challenges such as climate change and social justice, with shared interdisciplinary courses and Urban Lab projects with the City of Tampere.
programmes.overview: You study administrative sciences with attention to societal change and governance, in a programme that brings together urban development and sustainability across three specialisations: Administrative Sciences, Social Sciences and Technology. A challenge-based Urban Lab course puts students from the specialisations in teams on real urban development projects with organisations such as the City of Tampere. Graduates work in city organisations responsible for urban development and international affairs, in research projects and in companies focused on urban planning, with study rights to the master's programme in transformative urban and regional governance.
programmes.selectionNote: Group II: IB grades on the national administrative and social sciences table, 51% of places (about 5 of 10). Group I: SAT/ACT, 49%.

programmes.name: Social Sciences, Sustainable Urban Development
programmes.about: Social sciences for sustainable cities: theory of societal change plus real urban development projects in the Urban Lab.
programmes.overview: You study social sciences with a focus on societal change and how it affects wellbeing, equity, participation and environmental sustainability, within a programme that offers three specialisations: Administrative Sciences, Social Sciences and Technology. A challenge-based Urban Lab course puts you in interdisciplinary teams with local planners and citizens on real urban development projects with organisations such as the City of Tampere. Graduates work in public sector, city and regional organisations on development, planning and international affairs, or in research, and continue to the master's programme in social science research, in Transforming Societies or Comparative Social Policy and Welfare.
programmes.selectionNote: Group II: IB grades on the national administrative and social sciences table, 51% of places (about 5 of 10). Group I: SAT/ACT, 49%.

separateFrom.name: Administrative Sciences, Sustainable Urban Development
separateFrom.reason: A different degree (Bachelor of Social Sciences, not Administrative Sciences) with its own cut-off (54.5 against 65.6 points in 2026).

programmes.name: Technology, Sustainable Urban Development
programmes.about: Technology and engineering solutions for sustainable cities, with challenge-based Urban Lab courses run with partners such as the City of Tampere.
programmes.overview: You study technological and civil engineering solutions for sustainable built environments, in a programme that shares its Urban Lab course and its three specialisations (Technology, Administrative Sciences and Social Sciences) with students from other fields. In the challenge-based Urban Lab you work in interdisciplinary teams with local planners and citizens on real urban development projects with the City of Tampere and other organisations, and the degree ends with a thesis. Graduates have found work in city organisations, academia and engineering and technology companies, and continue to the master's programme in civil engineering with an urban systems focus.

programmes.name: Socially Sustainable Societies
programmes.about: Well-being, health and the Nordic welfare state: designing socially sustainable policies and institutions and reducing inequalities of income, gender, ethnicity, age and place.
programmes.overview: You examine well-being and health, past and present, through the social sciences, with themes in public health, urban studies and global social policy: welfare institutions, social protection, intergenerational justice and the reduction of inequality by income, gender, ethnicity, age and place. Teaching builds on the faculty's current research, and free-choice courses from other programmes let you broaden the degree. The programme takes a Nordic view of social sustainability and the welfare state. Graduates work in the public sector, corporations and non-governmental organisations, and continue to the master's tracks in Transforming Societies or Comparative Social Policy and Welfare.
programmes.selectionNote: Group I: SAT/ACT, 70% of places. Group II: IB grades on the national administrative and social sciences table, 30% (9 of 30).

notes: Every place is a 3+2 admission: finish the bachelor's and you continue to the matching Tampere master's without reapplying.
Programme-specific IB thresholds are listed only in each programme's admission criteria on Studyinfo.fi, so check them there.
If your predicted grades win you a place and your final grades fall below the threshold, the offer is withdrawn.
